newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grain prices mostly flat in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Grain prices mostly flat in Hungary.

text.p: Most grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) remained steady in minimal trade on Tuesday, with the exception of September milling wheat, dealers said.
"It was one of those rare days when there was a deal on the usually tradeless spot market for September milling wheat," said Janos Szolyka of Swap.

He said the spot deal at 29,200 forints per tonne was probably struck to cover a physical delivery and added that deliveries of August milling were being hampered by a number of quality problems, including low gluten content and a very high level of germination.
"Even if the gluten content is satisfactory, then the starch-to-sugar ratio is not right," Szolyka said. Weeds were another problem.
September milling wheat rose 330 forints per tonne to 28,630 and Szolyka said spot prices of around 27,000 forints were in line with current futures prices and further rises could not be excluded.
"Although a technical correction, even as large as 1,000 forints could happen, the underlying trend remains a rising one," he said. "But the market has to get used to these prices".

Milling wheat prices began to climb some three weeks ago when it became clear that despite a wheat crop of five million tonnes, well above last year's 3.9 million, there was little wheat that matched high BCE standards.
Total grains futures turnover was 318 lots, or 147 million forints, little changed from Monday's 293 lots.
August 20 is a market and public holiday in Hungary and trading on the BCE will resume on August 21.
